dropped.reason: Numerical artifact (float32 overflow). The head feeds pow_2_5(pow_1_5(Volume)), i.e. Volume^3.75, into a 30-day cross_corr. In float32, var_x*var_y overflows to inf, so the correlation comes out as exactly ±0. I ran the repo's rolling_pair_reduce on synthetic data: a stock whose 75th-percentile minute volume is above about 30k-50k shares gets zero (same window: f32 -0.0000, f64 -0.19). So a large slice of the cross-section, chosen by share volume, is pinned at 0, and the overflow dominates the ranking. Heavy-tailed F(1,3) values in x push the threshold even lower.

Numerical artifact (float32 overflow). In the outer 30-day correlation with Volume^3.75, var_y overflows to inf, so the correlation is exactly ±0. In the synthetic test, every stock with a 75th-percentile minute volume above about 50k-70k shares became zero, so the overflow dominates the ranking. The inner self-regression F is not the problem: measured exactly, it equals the 5-day sum of squared deviations divided by EPS.
